I just picked it up as I went, and was lucky enough to find a lot of good mentors along the way. If you want to start with minimal investment, get Ableton; that's what I use. Do internet searches on how to do stuff if you get stuck.
Out of curiosity, why Ableton over any other DAW?

It's just what I ended up using. Actually started with Fruity Loops (FL Studio), but it became somewhat limiting to use after a while, and wasn't as polished. Was making music with someone at the time who had Ableton and knew everything about it, so ended up going with that. It was also endorsed/used by a lot of musicians that I respected, so gave it a chance more than others. Did try Cubase for a while, but the interface was (IMO) way less intuitive and annoying.

Always did want to give Pro Tools a shot, but never got around to it. And this late in the game, not really sure I'd want to relearn a new DAW from scratch. If Ableton ever goes to shit, I'll reconsider, but in the mean time it just keeps getting better. I am using Ardour on linux, as well— trying to get a grip on it, so as to ditch Windows completely in the future. But that's a side project and not really investing a lot of time on it.

Anyway: it's very stable, compatible with nearly all VSTs and hardware, straight-forward/easy to understand, and there's an infinite amount of free online learning resources for it. It mostly comes down to personal preference and what you want to do with it; some DAWs are better suited to different tasks. For me: Ableton was simply at the right place, at the right time.
